title: Genetic Testing Results
alt: That's very exciting! The bad news is that it's a risk factor for a lot of things.
transcript:
[Cueball is seated on an medical examination table while Ponytail stands dressed in a doctor's coat holding a file in her right hand.]
Ponytail: Your genetic test results are back. Apparently you're part of an unbroken lineage stretching back billions of years to the early Earth!
explanation:
This comic is a direct continuation of the previous comic, 1839: Doctor Visit, where doctor Ponytail had checked Cueball's health. She has now done some testing for genetic risk factors.

s evaluate which genetic diseases people might be at risk for and/or give them insight into their ancestry. In this case, the genetic results are extremely obvious: his genes are part of a long line of genes stretching back to some of the earliest life forms to have genes. This information is universally true—every known organism has such a genetic history—which makes it so vague as to be useless for either medicine or ancestry. Every animal shares genes from the first living organism, known as LUCA ().

The title text says that being "part of an unbroken lineage stretching back billions of years" is a risk factor for a lot of things. In epidemiology, a risk factor is a variable associated with an increased risk of disease or infection. The title text says that this is a risk factor because being a living organism is, trivially, associated with every disease that exists.

The topic of risk factors would be covered again in 2620: Health Data. Genetic testing giving obvious results has been covered previously in 830: Genetic Analysis. A similar joke to the title text is seen in 674: Natural Parenting: "On one hand, every single one of my ancestors going back billions of years has managed to figure [having kids] out. On the other hand, that's the mother of all sampling biases."
